mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive divergence between real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and personal consumption expenditures (implied by GDPC1) over three months signals increased household savings and precautionary behavior, which typically precedes a consumer-driven equity rally and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > GDPC1 growth for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth outpaces GDPC1 growth for three consecutive months in a post-recession context.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate to below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is accelerating signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS growth accelerates for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which reduces GDP growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
